explanation.bottleneck: The source expresses transitions and outputs through full six-bit state comparisons and case selection. Depending on FSM extraction and mapping, these can introduce state-decode and selection depth on register-to-register paths and output paths.
explanation.rewrite: Retain six one-hot state registers but express their next-state functions directly as shallow sum-of-products equations. Share the mutually exclusive ten, twenty-without-ten, and idle input conditions. Decode outputs directly from the state bits, with a three-input OR for bill.
explanation.functional_boundaries: Preserves the module name, native ports, parameter declarations and defaults, one direct positive-edge clock, synchronous active-high clear, and Moore-output latency. Reset establishes exactly the ready state, and the equations preserve one-hot state membership for every subsequent input sequence, including arbitrary later clear assertions. ten retains priority when both payment inputs are high. No startup assumptions are added. Equivalence is required under the supplied startup contract and default ON/OFF values; behavior from arbitrary unreset illegal internal encodings is not claimed to match the original.
explanation.expected_timing_gain: The intended benefit is reduced state-decoding and mux depth. No improvement has been measured; synthesis may already optimize the original FSM similarly. Accept this candidate only after equivalence checking and fixed-setting EDA demonstrate strictly improved setup WNS, no TNS regression, and compliance with the area cap.
explanation.area_or_other_cost: Retains six state flip-flops and introduces no pipeline stages or dependencies. Direct state-bit outputs may reduce decoding area, while shared input conditions and synchronous-reset gating can affect fanout and mapping. Mapped area must be checked against 278.01664000000005 um^2.
